result.summary: Under the FLSA all time an employee is suffered or permitted to work is paid, except ordinary commuting and preliminary or postliminary activities excluded by the Portal-to-Portal Act; a de minimis exception exists.
Ordinary home-to-work travel is not hours worked, even to different worksites, unless the employee works during the trip.
Travel between job sites during the workday, or from the employer's premises to the first site after reporting, is hours worked.

Overnight travel away from home is hours worked only during the employee's normal working hours (including corresponding hours on non-working days); passenger time outside those hours is unpaid unless work is done.

Riding employer-provided transport from a meeting point to the worksite is not hours worked under the Portal-to-Portal Act unless the travel is itself a principal activity; several states (CA, NY, WA, MD, PA, MA) count it.

obligations.name: Equal pay
obligations.description: Employees doing the same or comparable work may not be paid differently because of a protected characteristic; some states also protect employees who discuss wages.

params.description: Characteristics the pay comparison protects

obligations.name: Exempt salary threshold
obligations.description: The lowest weekly salary at which an executive, administrative or professional employee may be treated as exempt from overtime; below it the employee is owed overtime regardless of duties.

params.description: Minimum weekly salary for the exemption

params.name: annual_salary
params.description: The same threshold expressed per year

obligations.name: Hours-worked standard
obligations.description: Which definition of compensable time governs in the jurisdiction: the FLSA with its Portal-to-Portal exclusions, a state regulation of its own, or a control test that counts any time under the employer's control.

params.name: standard
params.description: flsa_by_reference: the state adopts or defers to 29 CFR 785; state_regulation: the state has its own hours-worked rule (often close to federal but without some exclusions); control_test: any time subject to the employer's control is paid; no_state_law: only the FLSA applies

params.name: portal_to_portal_adopted
params.description: Whether the state excludes ordinary commuting and pre/post-shift activities the way 29 U.S.C. §254 does

params.name: notes

obligations.name: Pay frequency

params.name: minimum_frequency
params.description: Least frequent lawful pay schedule for the employees the rule covers; none means the state sets no frequency

params.name: max_days_between_paydays
params.description: Longest lawful gap between paydays where the statute counts days

params.description: Who the frequency rule covers when narrower than all employees

obligations.name: Workweek and workday definition

params.description: Length of the workweek in hours (168 = seven consecutive 24-hour periods)

params.name: workday_hours
params.description: Length of the workday where daily overtime applies (24 consecutive hours)

params.name: fixed_recurring
params.description: The period must be fixed and regularly recurring; changes are allowed only if permanent and not designed to evade overtime

obligations.name: Overtime premium
obligations.description: A multiple of the regular rate owed for hours past a daily or weekly threshold.

params.description: Hours after which the premium applies

params.name: period
params.description: Whether the threshold is per workday, per workweek, or applies to hours worked on the seventh consecutive day of the workweek
